rubric.why: Identifies who environmental education aims to enlighten.
rubric.description: Names people, particularly students, as the target of environmental education.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying people or students as the audience.

rubric.why: States the purpose as understanding the importance of protecting and conserving the environment.
rubric.description: Connects environmental education with the importance of environmental protection or conservation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it teaches the importance of protecting or conserving the environment.

modelAnswer: The objective of environmental education is to enlighten the people particularly the students, about the importance of protection and conservation of our environment.

rubric.why: Names damage to vegetation or the inability of plants to grow in acidic soil.
rubric.description: Explains that acid rain damages vegetation or makes soil too acidic for many plants to grow.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a stated effect on vegetation or plant growth.

rubric.why: Links loss of trees or roots to soil being washed away or eroded.
rubric.description: Explains that when trees are destroyed, the soil they hold together is washed away, preventing new plants from growing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the soil-loss consequence of tree destruction.

modelAnswer: Acid rain can damage vegetation and plants. Many plants cannot live or grow in acidic soil. Tree roots hold the soil together on hills and mountain areas.
If the trees are destroyed then the soil is washed away and new plants cannot grow there.

rubric.why: Identifies burning fossil fuels as the process that releases gases into the atmosphere.
rubric.description: States that burning fossil fuels releases harmful gases into the atmosphere.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking fossil-fuel burning with the release of gases.

rubric.why: Identifies sulphur in the fuels as the source of the harmful sulphur oxides.
rubric.description: Names SO₂ and SO₃ as gases produced due to sulphur in fossil fuels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying sulphur and at least one of the stated sulphur oxides.

modelAnswer: Burning of fossil fuels releases harmful gases into the atmosphere. These gases (SO₂, SO₃) are produced due to the presence of sulphur in the fossil fuels.

rubric.why: Identifies excessive use of agricultural chemicals as the harmful practice.
rubric.description: States that excessive use of insecticides, pesticides or other agricultural chemicals is harmful.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying excessive use of these chemicals.

rubric.why: States that birds are among the living things harmed.
rubric.description: Names birds as affected, with animals or human beings also acceptable as additional affected groups.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the chemicals harm birds.

modelAnswer: The excessive use of fertilizers, insecticides and pesticides, etc. for agriculture purposes has proved to be harmful for animals, birds and human beings.

rubric.why: Explains that unused carbon dioxide accumulates in the lower atmosphere and forms a dense layer.
rubric.description: States that carbon dioxide not used in photosynthesis accumulates in the lower atmosphere as a thick, dense layer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the accumulation and formation of the atmospheric layer.

rubric.why: Describes heat trapping by the layer and the resulting rise in Earth's average temperature.
rubric.description: Explains that the layer lets incoming solar radiation in but prevents it escaping, so Earth's average temperature rises.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the heat-trapping effect and resulting temperature rise.

modelAnswer: The remaining carbon dioxide which is not utilized in photosynthesis goes on accumulating in the lower areas of the atmosphere and forms a thick dense layer.
This layer behaves like glass sheet of greenhouse that allows the incoming solar radiation but does not allow it to escape outside; as a result of this the average temperature of the Earth rises.

rubric.why: States that acid rain acidifies soil and removes nutrients needed by plants.
rubric.description: Explains that acid rain makes soil more acidic and dissolves or washes away nutrients plants need.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the soil acidification or nutrient-loss effect.

rubric.why: Identifies toxic substances naturally present in soil that acid rain can dissolve.
rubric.description: Names aluminium or mercury as toxic substances that can be dissolved from the soil.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying toxic substances such as aluminium or mercury.

modelAnswer: Acid rain makes soil more acidic. It dissolves and washes away nutrients present in the soil which are needed by plants.
It can also dissolve toxic substances such as aluminium and mercury which are naturally present in the soil.
